groups.label: Add reversibility, detectability, and traceability to risk ratings
groups.desc: Expand the two-axis risk framework with factors such as reversibility, time to harm, error detectability, human review, and traceability to source evidence.

groups.label: Judge directiveness by behavior and discount disclaimers
groups.desc: Classify how directive a device is from what its outputs do, with rubrics or worked examples, and give no risk credit for disclaimers or labels alone.

groups.label: Ease rules for clinician supervised and informational tools
groups.desc: Place clinician-supervised or purely informational functions in lower risk tiers, streamlined pathways, or enforcement discretion.

groups.label: Publish a map from risk tier to required evidence
groups.desc: Publish guidance linking each risk position to the minimum evidence and clinical confirmation expected.

groups.label: Test devices across long conversations and repeated sessions
groups.desc: Evaluate behavior over whole conversations, late turns, repeated sessions, and stored user state instead of single prompts.

groups.label: Test whether outputs shift under user pressure
groups.desc: Benchmark whether advice changes with user affect, displeasure, reassurance, claimed authority, or beliefs when the clinical facts stay the same.

groups.label: Test for made up output when input is missing
groups.desc: Check that devices do not produce confident output when sensor, image, or other input is missing, broken, or null, and log such cases.

groups.label: Report under and over escalation separately
groups.desc: Report missed and unnecessary escalations as separate rates with prespecified, justified tolerances.

groups.label: Set separate pass or fail limits for critical failures
groups.desc: Set non-averageable thresholds for named high-consequence failures that a device must meet regardless of overall scores.

groups.label: Enforce safety rules outside the generative model
groups.desc: Use deterministic architecture and controls outside the model, and avoid relying on prompts, for scope limits and safety behaviors.

groups.label: Test for prompt injection, security, and dependency failures
groups.desc: Test resistance to prompt injection and cyber threats and verify safe behavior when connectivity, suppliers, or dependencies fail.

groups.label: Show benchmarks and reference ratings are valid and reliable
groups.desc: Require evidence that benchmarks measure what they claim, results reproduce across runs, datasets are documented, and human reference panels are qualified and agree.

groups.label: Use sequestered shared benchmarks and check contamination
groups.desc: Hold out sequestered or shared standard test sets, including ones qualified through FDA programs, and check for training-data contamination.

groups.label: Keep synthetic and real data results separate
groups.desc: Report synthetic and real-world results separately, validate synthetic data against real data, and do not let synthetic data alone set performance rates.

groups.label: Compare devices against realistic standards of care
groups.desc: Choose comparators that reflect the realistic alternative a patient would face, such as standard of care or no device, instead of a median clinician default.

groups.label: Evaluate clinicians and AI together as deployed
groups.desc: Measure performance of the human and device working together in the real workflow, alongside device-alone results.

groups.label: Show that human oversight works in practice
groups.desc: Credit human review only when testing shows users catch and override errors, including human factors and automation bias testing.

groups.label: Evaluate the full deployed system including prompts
groups.desc: Treat the exact deployed configuration, including prompts, retrieval, tools, and orchestration, as the thing tested and controlled.

groups.label: Test across populations, settings, and atypical cases
groups.desc: Evaluate performance across subgroups, children, rural and low-resource settings, and hard or out-of-distribution cases.

groups.label: Require prospective outcome studies for high risk devices
groups.desc: Require prospective clinical studies measuring patient outcomes or clinical utility for high-risk or action-directing devices.

groups.label: Restrict trading premarket evidence for postmarket monitoring
groups.desc: Allow reduced premarket evidence only for low-risk functions where failures are detectable and reversible and monitoring is in place.

groups.label: Prespecify postmarket triggers, thresholds, and responses
groups.desc: Make postmarket monitoring plans enforceable with set metrics, thresholds, cadence, event triggers, and corrective actions.

groups.label: Monitor for drift and unannounced model changes
groups.desc: Detect performance drift and silent upstream model changes after launch with canary tests, golden suites, or output monitoring.

groups.label: Monitor with records the device cannot alter
groups.desc: Base monitoring and evidence on independent records outside the device's control instead of the device's own self-reports.

groups.label: Retest against the baseline whenever the model changes
groups.desc: Re-run benchmarks against the premarket baseline before deploying any model, prompt, or configuration change.

groups.label: Pin model versions and require notice of changes
groups.desc: Lock foundation model versions, forbid silent updates, and require advance notice of supplier model changes.

groups.label: Limit preapproved change plans to bounded changes
groups.desc: Define predetermined change control plans as bounded envelopes or categories of change with set verification and rollback.

groups.label: Require model developers to share model information
groups.desc: Require foundation model developers to disclose model information through master files, contracts, or model cards, with manufacturers characterizing models otherwise.

groups.label: Keep accountability clear and centered on manufacturers
groups.desc: Keep manufacturers responsible for model validity and monitoring despite master files or deployers, and assign clear legal accountability for harms.

groups.label: Keep records for audit and incident review
groups.desc: Keep logs that can reconstruct events, including the model version, configuration, and human decisions behind each output.

groups.label: Require human approval before consequential or irreversible actions
groups.desc: Require a qualified human to approve consequential clinical decisions and irreversible agentic actions before they happen.

groups.label: Define and enforce limits on agent authority
groups.desc: Specify what agentic devices may access and do, enforce least privilege, and check permissions at the time of each action.

groups.label: Test agents across the full sequence of actions
groups.desc: Evaluate agentic systems on their whole action trajectory, including retries and delegation, beyond final endpoints.

groups.label: Validate supervisory AI agents and keep human review
groups.desc: Validate AI monitors independently of the device they supervise, using different models, and keep them below human review.

groups.label: Require a tested off switch and rollback
groups.desc: Require tested ways to stop, suspend, or roll back a device or agent quickly.

groups.label: Tell patients when AI shapes their care
groups.desc: Disclose to patients, and seek consent where needed, when AI substantially participates in their care.

groups.label: Protect patient data and limit secondary use
groups.desc: Protect patient data, treat data sensitivity as a risk factor, and limit collection, retention, and secondary uses such as training.

groups.label: Clarify and expand reporting of AI errors and harms
groups.desc: Clarify adverse event reporting for generative errors and gradual harms and give patients and clinicians channels to report problems.

groups.label: Require independent third party evaluation
groups.desc: Require or accredit independent evaluators, free of conflicts, to test devices instead of relying only on sponsor testing.

groups.label: Align terms and standards across agencies and countries
groups.desc: Use consistent AI terminology across FDA and other agencies and harmonize with international and existing standards.

groups.label: Include nurses and other non-physician clinicians in evaluation
groups.desc: Treat nurses, nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, and other non-physician clinicians as intended users, use function-based clinician terms, and include them as evaluators, comparators, and adjudicators and in developing rules.
